page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio, alongside 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU provides advanced instruction set support, including AVX-512 extensions (VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-threaded performance contrasted with modest multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests such as stress-ng (3,602.88) and Geekbench single-core (2,009.0) rank in the top tiers, complemented by high-throughput single-threaded compression reaching 39.24 GB/sec in gzip. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics show limitations tied to its 4-vCPU ceiling, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,367.0 and lower relative compilation speeds under Clang. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 69.83 GB/sec for reads and 41.08 GB/sec for writes, providing steady throughput for memory-bound execution.

The primary operational tradeoff of the vx1-g-4c-16g is its minimal local NVMe footprint of 1 GB, necessitating network-attached block storage or external persistence for data-heavy applications. Given its balanced compute and memory profile alongside competitive single-core speed, this server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, microservices, lightweight web serving, Redis caching nodes, and small-model machine learning inference tasks.
description: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g is a VX1 Cloud Compute instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical AMD EPYC cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the processor integrates modern vector instructions including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators. Benchmarks highlight upper-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong single-threaded data compression, though total multi-threaded output reflects its 4-vCPU capacity. Memory read bandwidth sustains 69.83 GB/sec uncached, supporting predictable data access. Due to the restricted 1 GB boot and storage volume, instances typically require external block storage volumes for persistent data. The instance provides a balanced configuration optimal for general-purpose workloads, API and web servers, caching layers, and lightweight background task processing.
